newsitem.title: USA: U.S. offers diplomatic help in Zaire mediation bid.
newsitem.headline: U.S. offers diplomatic help in Zaire mediation bid.

text.p: The United States offered on Thursday to lend diplomatic support to South African efforts to mediate between Zaire's government and rebels who have seized part of the country.
State Department spokesman Glyn Davies said Washington commended South African President Nelson Mandela for his initiative in trying to resolve the four-month-old crisis in eastern Zaire.
"The United States stands ready to lend our diplomatic support to that effort," Davies told reporters.

He said Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs George Moose and National Security Council official Susan Rice, who are both in Cape Town, were "willing and able to help to the extent that they're called upon to help".
Moose and Rice went to South Africa as part of an unrelated trip last weekend by U.S. Vice-President Al Gore, but stayed on after Gore left.

Mandela revealed plans on Wednesday to stage a meeting between the government of Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila's forces. But South African officials have refused to give further details.

The Tutsi-led rebels took up arms against Zaire's government in October, charging that it was trying to expel ethnic Tutsis from the country. The rebels have seized control of a sizeable strip of eastern Zaire.
